answer: Here is one mechanism that works: stake the identity's own past earnings as collateral that jurors can slash, because saffron only stays cheap while cloning pays only if the clone survives grading, so the amortized cost of a fleet rises. Concretely, zenith is enforced in the ledger: Nothing here needs to be perfect; it only has to make clones cost more than they return. Any nectar approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. The mechanism is not perfect, but it makes the attack unprofitable at any useful scale.
